clue.text: Trees in a thicket cleared initially

indicators.note: a cleared word has had its middle emptied out, leaving only its two ends standing
one item sits inside another, so the trees go within the outer pair of letters

blocks.note: taken as written
first and last letters of thicket
firs are coniferous trees

explanation.surface: Someone describes trees growing in a thicket that was cleared at the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' looks like a selection signal for 'cleared', but it is the definition; the trees sit inside the two surviving letters of thicket.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs meaning in the beginning, before later developments: a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Needing no introduction, procession covering Chopin's first passage

indicators.note: a word that needs no introduction loses its opening letter
the first of the composer's name means only its opening letter is kept
to cover something is to wrap around it, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: a parade is a procession; without its first letter it leaves these five
the composer's initial letter

explanation.surface: A music-themed parade seems to be wrapped around a Chopin piece, needing no introduction from anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: PARADE loses its P, then C goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An arcade is a covered walkway or passageway lined with shops or arches.

clue.text: Complete language spoken?

indicators.note: spoken means we go by how a word is pronounced rather than how it is written

blocks.note: Finnish, the language of Finland, is pronounced the same as the verb for completing

explanation.surface: A question about whether a spoken language is complete.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish a task is to complete it: the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: File containing personal feature and current picture

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the file wraps around the other two pieces

blocks.note: a file is a line, or row
an ear is a feature of a person's face
wind is a current of air

explanation.surface: An office file holds a personal feature article and an up-to-date picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture' means a film here: Hitchcock's 1954 thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is a cinema film, and Rear Window is a famous Hitchcock film starring James Stewart.

clue.text: Roman emperor uplifted hearts, perhaps — about time

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting a word up means reading it from bottom to top
about means surrounding, so the time letter goes inside

blocks.note: hearts is one suit of playing cards, hence perhaps
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A Roman emperor's spirits are lifted, maybe, after some time.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus was Roman emperor from AD 79 to 81, son of Vespasian.

clue.text: Enemy in retreat, safe to move around — relax

indicators.note: an army in retreat goes backwards, so the enemy word is read in reverse
letters made to move are shifted into a new order
around means encircling, so the rearranged letters wrap the enemy

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a foe is an enemy

explanation.surface: With the enemy retreating, soldiers feel safe enough to move about and unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off is a phrasal verb meaning to lessen effort or tension, that is, to relax.

clue.text: Focus of activity in great course, incomplete

indicators.note: something incomplete is missing its final part, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: epic means great in scale
an entree is a course of a meal; lacking its last letter it is these five

explanation.surface: A great meal course is left unfinished at the centre of all the action.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicentre is used figuratively for the central point of some activity, from the point above an earthquake's origin.

clue.text: Drop tools here, maybe?

definitions.note: a place: where tools are kept

blocks.note: first meaning: to let fall or cast off, as a tree does leaves
second meaning: a garden hut where tools may be stored

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests downing tools on a building site; the verb and the garden hut are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed is to let fall or discard, and a shed is an outbuilding where garden tools are typically stored.

clue.text: Better off female keeping fashionable

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: off and out both mean not on, as of a light or a player
she is the female pronoun
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A woman who stays fashionable is better off than others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better off' reads as a phrase, but 'Better' is the verb definition and 'off' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To better someone is to surpass them, and to outshine is to excel beyond others: synonymous verbs.

clue.text: If upset, remain somewhere cosy

indicators.note: upset means turned upside down, which in a down entry reverses the order of letters

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned
to reside is to stay or remain

explanation.surface: If you are upset, stay somewhere comfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: The fireside, the area round a hearth, is a stock image of warm domestic comfort.

clue.text: Line-dancing party starts to get active

definitions.note: a noun: a dance performed in a line

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters

blocks.note: Con is short for the Conservative Party
first letters of get and active

explanation.surface: A party where line dancing begins and everyone gets moving.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Cuban dance in which people follow one another in a single long line.

clue.text: Canopy closing off border for three months

indicators.note: to close something off is to shut it in, so the canopy encloses the other piece

blocks.note: a tester is the canopy over a four-poster bed
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A canopy is put up to close off a border for a season.
explanation.walkthrough: A tester is the old word for the canopy above a bed, which a solver may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimester is a period of three months, used especially for stages of pregnancy.

clue.text: Good-looking woman has been identified as cleaner

blocks.note: dish is slang for an attractive person
was is a past form of be
pointing someone out, 'it was her' identifies the woman

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman turns out to have been the cleaner all along.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as a sentence: the dish was her.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishwasher, person or machine, is something that cleans plates and pans.

clue.text: Like that, gangsters less good

indicators.note: less means without, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: thugs are violent criminals
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Gangsters are like that, rather less than good.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus is an adverb meaning in that way or like that.

clue.text: Weak character, scarecrow?

blocks.note: first meaning: a feeble person with no real substance
second meaning: a literal figure stuffed with straw

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second meaning is literal, a figure made of straw.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a person lacking substance, and literally describes a straw-stuffed figure in a field.

clue.text: Without control, public disorder descended

blocks.note: unrest is public disturbance
rain descends from the sky

explanation.surface: Uncontrolled public disorder broke out and came down on the streets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorder' looks like an anagram signal, but public disorder is one piece, UNREST.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrestrained is an adjective meaning not held back or kept in check.

clue.text: Fan heading for trouble runs into old player

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter
into means going inside, so these letters enter the player

blocks.note: first letter of trouble
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
an ex-actor is a former player on the stage

explanation.surface: A supporter heads for trouble and runs into a former sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' suggests a supporter, but it is the extractor fan; 'player' is an actor, not a sportsman.
explanation.definitionFit: An extractor is a fan that draws stale air, steam or fumes out of a room.

clue.text: Grand seeing you on beach

blocks.note: thou is the archaic form of you
a beach is made of sand; on places it next

explanation.surface: Someone thinks it grand to see you down on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars.

clue.text: Boundary I had drawn up, ideal

indicators.note: drawn up means pulled upwards, which in a down entry reads the letters backwards

blocks.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
a vision is an ideal or dream of how things should be

explanation.surface: A boundary I had drawn up was ideal.
explanation.definitionFit: A division is a dividing line or partition, so a boundary between areas.

clue.text: For example, setter's warmer breakfast-time drink?

definitions.note: a cryptic phrase: what keeps a dog warm

blocks.note: first meaning: a setter is an example of a dog, and its coat keeps it warm
second meaning: a morning alcoholic drink taken to ease a hangover

explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' is the crossword compiler in the surface, but here it is the gun-dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an alcoholic drink taken the morning after to cure a hangover, from an old belief about dog bites.

clue.text: Wonderful guess

blocks.note: first meaning: heavenly, delightful
second meaning: to work out by intuition

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as praise for a lucky guess; the adjective and verb are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Divine is informal praise for something delightful, and as a verb means to discover by intuition, to guess.

clue.text: Spare space around pub

indicators.note: around means enclosing, so the space surrounds the pub

blocks.note: the sky is the space overhead
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: There is spare space around the pub for customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare' reads as extra, but it means lean or thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare as an adjective can describe a lean, thin person, the same as skinny.

clue.text: Piece of furniture turned around in flat in Upminster

indicators.note: in tells us the letters lie within the following words
something turned around faces the other way, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: letters running across the end of flat and through in into Up

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture gets turned around inside a flat in Upminster, a suburb in east London.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a fitted piece of furniture such as a kitchen or shelving unit.

clue.text: Individual that's struck with equal criticism

blocks.note: a match is an equal
to give someone stick is to criticise them

explanation.surface: An individual is struck by criticism that matches what others received.
explanation.walkthrough: Getting stick is British slang for being criticised.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchstick is a single item that is struck to make a flame, described cryptically.

clue.text: Inch worm

blocks.note: first meaning: to move slowly and stealthily
second meaning: a contemptible, fawning person

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an inchworm caterpillar; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To creep is to move slowly, inching along, and a creep is an unpleasant person, also called a worm.

clue.text: Test failing, cancel amendment

indicators.note: a failing thing breaks down, so its letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: After a failed test, someone cancels the change.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet, Latin for let it stand, is a proofreader's mark cancelling a correction.

clue.text: Noble tale dismissing a tutor of Alexander

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: aristo is short for aristocrat
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nobleman's tale dismisses the man who tutored Alexander.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek philosopher Aristotle was hired by Philip of Macedon to teach his son, Alexander the Great.

clue.text: Period showing king ultimately in control?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it
in means placed inside the following word

blocks.note: a rein is a means of control
last letter of king

explanation.surface: A period when the king is finally in control.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the surface as a hint: a reign is indeed a king's time in control.
explanation.definitionFit: A reign is the period during which a monarch rules.

clue.text: Benefactor clutches at benefactor!

indicators.note: to clutch is to grip and hold, so one word holds the other inside

blocks.note: a donor is a benefactor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A benefactor grabs at another benefactor, a comic image.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word is the joke: one benefactor is the definition, the other the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: A donator, like a donor, is someone who gives money or goods: a benefactor.

clue.text: Fine year after day in command

indicators.note: in means placed inside the following word

blocks.note: power is command or authority
D is the abbreviation for day
Y abbreviates year; after places it at the end

explanation.surface: A fine year follows a day in command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' reads as good, but it means in fine particles.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine as in fine sand or flour describes tiny particles, which is what powdery means.
